To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

women leave academic medicine because of a lack of role models, research difficulties, work–life balance challenges, and a perceived institutional environment that is noncollaborative, biased, and undervalues their contributions to the institution.
women physicians who leave academic medicine report that they are dissatisfied with the institutional culture and feel that they are not recognized for their contributions.

the lack of role models, frustration with the research environment and work-life balance, and the perceived institutional culture were the key factors that influenced women to leave academic medicine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why women leave academic medicine.
the reasons why women physicians leave academic medicine.
the experiences of women physicians who have left careers in academic medicine, with a focus on understanding why they left and how they perceive the academic environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
women in academic medicine are not valued for their work and that they are not valued for the work that they do.
women are leaving academic medicine in large numbers and that they are leaving for reasons that are not well understood.
there are many factors involved in women leaving academic medicine and the reasons are not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

women physicians who leave academic medicine do not do so because of a lack of commitment to their work, but rather because of a perceived lack of institutional support and recognition for the work that they do.

women are more likely than men to leave academia for reasons of work-life balance and that they are also less likely than men to be in a relationship with another physician, which may be a protective factor against leaving.
the women physicians interviewed were able to identify a number of factors that contributed to their decision to leave academia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
women physicians in academic medicine need to feel that they have the support of their institutions in order to thrive in their careers and to stay in academic medicine.
the institutional culture of academic medicine is not conducive for many women.
women are leaving academic medicine because they do not feel valued.
